title: Pulse Runner core experience

audience.description: Players who want an immediately readable, short-session arcade challenge with room for movement mastery.
needs: understand the goal without a tutorial wall
feel responsible for both successful collections and avoidable damage
see useful improvement across repeated short runs
exclusions: players seeking idle or low-attention play

playerExperience.fantasy: Thread a nimble runner through a hostile neon arena and turn controlled risk into momentum.

pillars.statement: Every threat, reward, and movement consequence remains readable at arcade speed.
Better scores come from visible risks that the player elects to take.
A complete attempt is short, but movement skill produces measurable improvement.

antiPillars: waiting for the game to become interesting
visual noise that hides collision intent

coreLoop.description: Read the arena, choose a pulse route, evade moving drones, collect for score, and immediately retry with better control.

mustPreserve: short-session top-down movement remains the primary interaction
threat and collision consequences remain readable
a failed or completed attempt can restart immediately
freeToExplore: the player movement model and its expressive techniques
hazard behaviors, formations, and encounter rhythms
reward placement, value, movement, and respawn logic
risk, combo, multiplier, and recovery systems
camera, animation, audio, and feedback treatments

explorationQuestions.question: What creates player-chosen risk without making damage feel arbitrary?
explorationQuestions.whyItMatters: Chosen risk is a pillar, but the implementation should emerge from prototypes rather than a prescribed reward pattern.
signals: players can explain why damage happened
higher rewards correlate with voluntary exposure

explorationQuestions.question: How can players with different priorities develop distinct, successful styles?
explorationQuestions.whyItMatters: A single dominant route would make the synthetic personas and repeated runs less meaningful.
signals: multiple routes or tactics remain competitive
improvement is not only faster input

explorationQuestions.question: What teaches the core loop through play in the first few seconds?
explorationQuestions.whyItMatters: The audience wants immediate readability without a tutorial wall.
signals: the objective becomes apparent without prose

hypotheses.predictedDynamic: A sufficiently expressive movement model lets skilled players pursue aggressive routes while novices can still correct obvious mistakes.
falsifiers: optimizer and novice traces become indistinguishable

hypotheses.predictedDynamic: Legible reward opportunities cause players to trade safe positioning for more valuable routes.
hypotheses.intendedExperience: Tension followed by relief and earned momentum.
evidence: pickups and damage move together across personas
falsifiers: the safest persona also collects the most

personas.label: Hesitant novice
personas.description: Pursues the obvious nearby reward, reacts slowly, and underweights danger.

personas.label: Score optimizer
personas.description: Routes directly toward the nearest pulse while making fast, efficient hazard corrections.

personas.label: Risk-averse survivor
personas.description: Prioritizes space from drones and only weakly pursues the nearest reward.

accessibility: movement must support keyboard directional input without simultaneous button chords
critical objects cannot rely on color alone in a production art pass
damage feedback must have a non-flashing alternative
performance: maintain 60 Hz simulation on the desktop target
avoid per-frame allocations in the core arena loop

unknowns: whether first-time players understand pulse collection without reading the help line
whether the 45-second production round sustains interest after the short automated slices
whether damage and collection feel fair to humans with different motor abilities

metadata.changePolicy: Version and re-baseline personas before changing pillars, hypotheses, or quality bars.
